checks.evidence: The span refusal, its acceptance cases and the MixedVertices refusal are proven in query_language planning/service_test.rs. The schema-side vertex check is proven in execution_domain operation_schema/service_test.rs. The harness tests are in cli/tests/replay/recordings.rs, including a_golden_rule_that_is_not_recorded_fails. Nothing rests on benchmarks/ or languages/.

refuse_spans_alone fires for all eleven kinds, and the over-refusal cases keep a span with a file key. refuse_mixed_vertices (planning/service.rs:277-302) refuses a located closure or cycles step at compile time (assembling/service.rs:121-122). Harness-leak lens: F1-F5 and L1 are closed. golden_strays (answers.rs:544-556) fails any findings.toml key that names no recording, and is wired into the `names` replay answer (behavior.rs:52). The digest is removed. No remaining path turns a failure into a pass: required files, strict tables and keys, strict counts, exact undecided rows, pending matched to the actual refusal, every row and every golden key tied to a live recording. The all-rules proof is a cross-branch dependency on claude/w13-bench-parity.
refuse_spans_alone and refuse_mixed_vertices are pub(crate), LoweringError is pub(crate), and same_vertices is private. The harness helpers are pub(crate) in the cli test fixtures only.

Span equality is value equality in every kernel, and held_inside_one_file is the one placement site naming Span. The vertex-kind rule is checked at compile time for a located refusal (refuse_mixed_vertices) and in the engine's schema contract for any plan, hand-built ones included (same_vertices). These are two layers of one shape contract, as with the existing span-operand checks, not two representations of one concept.
The new refusal stays in the query_language domain (planning, lowering errors, assembling); compile and typecheck map the error in their inbound services. No layer is crossed.
The new tests are cfg(test) or under cli/tests; no production-reachable seam is added.

findings: cross-branch dependency: the ruff_parity all-rules proof cited in the query_language README resolves through claude/w13-bench-parity, which must commit or regenerate its staged request and assert that selected_rules equals the 413 configured rules.

verified closed across the passes: kernel inference W1-W9; union, intersection and difference; over-refusal acceptance for every kind (cycles trivially, since it has no key slot); replay harness leaks H1-H9, F1-F5, L1; digest M1; located vertex refusal M2.
